claims.text: OpenAI RSS timestamped publication of the quantum-computing experiment case at 2026-09-08T17:00:00Z.

The technical case study is authored by MIT and OpenAI researchers, dated 4 September 2026, with MIT authors developing the infrastructure and running experiments and OpenAI authors advising on agent infrastructure and text.
claims.sourceLocator: PDF title page and Contributions, pages 1 and 10

claims.text: The reported agent used GPT-5.6 Sol at Ultra reasoning level through Codex, EQuS orchestration software and a simple in-house Jupyter MCP.
The tested previously unmeasured chip contained six uncoupled qubits, four fixed-frequency and two tunable, each paired with a readout resonator.
The agent found all six resonators and suitable initial readout powers.
Across 40 target measurements for four fixed-frequency qubits, researchers report intervening to improve four.
The completed fixed-qubit sequence included transition-frequency, pulse-calibration, readout and coherence measurements.
claims.sourceLocator: Launch-page lines 31-36; PDF pages 5-6 and Figure 5 caption

claims.text: The reported work controlled live laboratory hardware rather than a simulation.
The case-study authors describe the chip as relatively simple and the measurements as standard and much simpler than a novel multi-qubit experiment.
The case study says an experienced researcher can probably reach suitable calibration settings faster while working continuously.
Researchers spent several months refining the setup context, chip designs, measurement-specific skills and source-code access used by the agent.
Measurement skills could include template code, prerequisites, parameter-selection advice, likely physical failure modes, success and failure criteria and example plots.
OpenAI says EQuS now regularly uses agents to help with routine chip characterisation.

For a weak tunable-qubit signal, the agent needed substantial researcher guidance. A wider-sweep prompt and suggested parameters preceded a finer scan that the agent incorrectly accepted; the final improvement followed a separate request for another fine scan, identification that the spectrum had likely fallen outside the scanned range, and wider follow-up scans.
claims.sourceLocator: PDF pages 7-8, Figure 6 panels B-G and caption

claims.text: The case study says agents were anecdotally slower than experienced researchers even when they converged, and serial physical acquisition limits parallel brute-force exploration.
An independent 2025 Patterns paper predates the OpenAI/MIT case and reported a different agent framework for superconducting-qubit experiments.
claims.sourceLocator: OpenAI/MIT references page 10; Patterns publication date and Results

claims.text: The Patterns experiment used a 16-qubit processor and selected three adjacent qubits for its demonstration.
The Patterns paper reported automated single-qubit recalibration, two-qubit gate calibration and a three-qubit GHZ-state experiment.
The Patterns paper reported 97 per cent accuracy for GPT-4o on one instruction-translation benchmark, with failed code retried in practice.
The Patterns system depended on orderly code and procedure documentation, which the authors identified as a human-effort and transfer limitation.
The Patterns implementation allowed termination of the whole program on an external or emergency signal but lacked fine-grained interruption inside execution.

The Argonne instrument-agent paper constrained model variability through restricted instrument-specific functions, automated linting, human oversight and administrator execution while keeping low-level control deterministic and validated.
The Argonne system handled omitted required parameters through approved defaults or a clarification request rather than model inference.
The transferable deployment result is the complete model, skills, orchestration, data-access, write and intervention loop rather than GPT-5.6 Sol in isolation.

claims.text: A practical laboratory evaluation should separately test model decision scope, executable actions, persisted state, stop and clarification conditions, intervention burden and robustness to environmental change.

claims.text: The case supports evaluating GPT-5.6 Sol as a component for bounded routine laboratory work, but does not establish a ready-made autonomous scientist.
